tagline: Self-hosted helpdesk and ticketing platform handling email, chat, phone and social channels.
description: Zammad is a web-based helpdesk for customer support. It collects requests from email, chat, telephone and social media into one ticket system, and the docs describe a knowledge base, a REST API and service-level agreements. The code is Ruby on Rails with a Vue front end, released under AGPLv3 and owned by the independent Zammad Foundation. Zammad GmbH, the company behind it, sells a cloud service. You can self-host with Docker Compose images, a Helm chart for Kubernetes, DEB and RPM packages, or from source. The docs require PostgreSQL 15 or newer and Redis 7 or newer, and strongly recommend Elasticsearch for search. As a rough guide, the minimum is 2 CPU cores and 6 GB of RAM, with 4 GB more if Elasticsearch runs on the same server. The example setup for up to 40 agents uses 6 cores. Zammad is a close match for Zendesk on multichannel tickets, so the main cost of switching is running the servers yourself rather than any missing core feature.
strengths: Brings email, chat, telephone and social media requests into a single ticket queue
Has a documented REST API with endpoints for tickets, users, groups, SLAs and the knowledge base
Installs from Docker Compose, a Helm chart, DEB or RPM packages, or source
Owned by an independent foundation, and the maintainers state the software stays AGPLv3
Docs give sizing guidance, including an example setup for up to 40 agents
limits: Needs about 2 CPU cores and 6 GB of RAM at minimum, plus 4 GB more for a local Elasticsearch
Requires PostgreSQL 15 or newer and Redis 7 or newer
Without Elasticsearch, search is very limited, so a full setup has one more service to run
The documented example for 40 agents uses 6 CPU cores, so a growing team has to plan server capacity
bestFor: A support team of roughly 5 to 40 agents with a sysadmin who wants a Zendesk-style multichannel helpdesk on its own servers.
